subject: Multipool reservation + isolation: qualification summary & MAP
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sylvia Kim <sylvia.kim@hearthai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 18:32:00 -0700
Subject: Multipool reservation + isolation: qualification summary & MAP

Sylvia — thanks again for taking the call today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the constraints you shared, and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) to keep momentum toward a reserved/multipool proof point. Please flag anything I mis-stated.

High-level pain & goals
- Peak production: ~600 concurrent inference lanes during weekday peak for conversation agents (avg token length 75–120).
- Cost predictability: Procurement needs a clear committed SKU and predictable monthly unit cost for budgeting.
- Data isolation: PHI-adjacent PII; you require tenant isolation (single-tenant pool) for a subset of traffic and multi-tenant for lower-sensitivity bursts.
- SLA target: 99.95% monthly uptime; p95 latency target < 180ms for prompt length <= 256 tokens.

Technical constraints we noted
- Sequence lengths skew long on recommendation flows (up to 2k tokens occasionally) — KV cache sizing and kernel selection matter.
- On-prem for batch training calls is out; you want Redwood Private for the PHI flow (VPC).
- Procurement window: decision expected by end of Q3; initial PO for 6–9 months preferred.

Redwood proposal summary (high level)
- Dedicated multipool: 2x single-tenant pools (for PHI-sensitive agents) sized for 200 lanes each, plus a shared pool for burst ~200 lanes.
- Autoscale/burst: configurable burst to hosted capacity during non-business-critical windows; local fallback to quantized variants for cost control.
- Ops & SLAs: 99.95% uptime SLA for Dedicated, included runbook and two-week ramp validation (canary).

Next-step MAP (owner / timing)
1) Redwood sends a scoped estimate + MOP draft (Jonas) — EOD Wed 2027-06-23.
2) HearthAI to share procurement contact and desired contract term (Sylvia) — by Fri 2027-06-25.
3) Technical deep-dive with Karthik + HearthAI infra team to validate throughput (30–45 min) — target week of 6/28.
4) Draft SOW/PO review and quick pricing iteration (Ben) — after technical sign-off.

Attachments: estimate + initial MAP draft attached.

If that looks good, I’ll queue the technical slot with Karthik for early next week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Jonas — this is a great summary and captures the key constraints. Two quick clarifications:

1) Pool sizing: can we model a conservative lane utilization (70% busy factor) when you produce the estimate? We want to avoid over-commitment but also give ops breathing room.
2) SLA: 99.95% is the target, but our security team will want a clear incident escalation path and log retention window (12 months). Can you include that in the MOP?

Procurement contact: procurement@hearthai.com (cc’d). They’ll own term negotiation and vendor onboarding. Liam (infra) will coordinate the deep-dive — he’s cc’d.

Sylvia

Looping in a quick pricing/ops note from the commercial side. Thanks for the MAP — a couple commercial clarifications to speed PO prep:

- Commitment term: we can do a 6 or 12 month reserved SKU. 6-month term gives flexibility; 12-month offers a ~12% unit discount.
- Burst model: we recommend a soft-burst allowance (up to 25% extra capacity) without enforcing capacity preemption during business hours; hard burst applies off-hours.
- Pricing artifact: attached is a simple cost table that aligns with the 70% utilization baseline and the 60/70/85 sensitivity Jonas mentioned. It also includes an example PO line item for the single-tenant pools.

Action items from Ben
- I’ll produce a clean pricing table (line items + example PO) and route to procurement@hearthai.com by Fri 6/25 EOD.
- If HearthAI prefers a 12-month term, we can draft a term sheet with the 12% discount and SLA language for review.
